flawed_step: The step 'contract the triangle and take a 3-edge-colouring of the contracted graph' cannot be justified. Contracting a triangle gives a smaller bridgeless cubic graph, but nothing guarantees that graph is 3-edge-colourable. Only the lifting direction is valid, and it runs both ways, so G is colourable exactly when G/T is.
counterexample: Take the Petersen graph and replace one vertex by a triangle (truncate it). The result is simple (Petersen has girth 5), cubic, contains a triangle, and is bridgeless (truncation keeps 3-edge-connectivity). Suppose it had a 3-edge-colouring. The triangle's edges would get three distinct colours, and each pendant edge would get the colour of the opposite triangle edge. So the three edges leaving the triangle would have distinct colours, and contracting the triangle would give a 3-edge-colouring of the Petersen graph, which is impossible.
assessment_summary: Contracting a triangle shows that G is 3-edge-colourable exactly when G/T is. It does not show that G/T is colourable, and the argument has no base case or induction that would supply this. Blowing up one vertex of the Petersen graph into a triangle gives a bridgeless cubic simple graph with a triangle that has no 3-edge-colouring. So the statement is false.
